title: Visa’s 7-year obsession: “the public can’t public”
summary:
It starts with visakanv dropping the cleanest doomer bumper-sticker imaginable: **“The public is insufficiently educated on how to be a good public.”** And then he spends the next several years basically pointing at every internet-pathology and going “see? it’s *this* again.” His specific claim is that modern life is a tragedy-of-the-commons situation where the public gets trained to obey/consume, media incentives juice anxiety and outrage, and a tiny number of “assholes” can wreck whole spaces because everyone’s bad at recognizing them *and* coordinating against them without turning into rage-monsters themselves (his infamous “assholes are 1% causing 74% of the problems” riff). The extra sting: smart people often stay silent because the downside of speaking publicly is catastrophic, which “really sucks for smart kids in shitty social graphs.”

The arc is basically: **[2018 seed tweet] → [2019 peak: applied rants + “bouncer skills”] → [2020 reboot + gradual shift toward “just build your own graph”] → [2024–2025 comms theory + resignation-with-practice]**. 2019 is the peak because he keeps translating the thesis into practical sub-doctrines: journaling as “radical self-ownership” (set your own curriculum instead of “journaling for corporate masters”), “write stupid, edit smart” for creative output, and the big comms move: “communication is lossy” and the real failure is people not appreciating that—so they don’t give others room to revise. The SSC culture-war blowup is his favorite case study: he frames Scott Alexander’s openness as an “idealism experiment” that only works if communities learn to neutrally eject contemptuous actors (“imagine a cool, collected bouncer… we need to collectively develop that skillset”).

By 2020–2024 you can see the emotional outcome: he’s still yelling about the broken public, but he’s also openly steering toward **“tend to your own social graph”** (find good people, enforce house rules, build high-trust semi-public spaces) because the big “educate the public” project is a morale trap. Malcolm_Ocean pops up as the recurring echo/booster (pointing to Schmachtenberger, noticing how QT-able the seed tweet is, joking about printing it on a shirt), and Rusty_Swarf later puts a name to the vibe shift: public-education is an **“infinite sink”** that diffuses your effort and makes you feel hopeless—better to focus on tangible relationships and let the sink capture whatever upside. The residue is that Visa basically gave his corner of Twitter a mini vocabulary pack—**“asshole problem,” “bouncer skills,” “comms is lossy,” “design your echo chamber,” “tend your graph”**—that people keep reusing anytime a platform meltdown or public freakout happens.
